newsitem.title: UK: UK police arrest man wanted for Cyprus car bomb.
newsitem.headline: UK police arrest man wanted for Cyprus car bomb.

text.p: British police said on Friday they had arrested a 45-year-old Cypriot man wanted in connection with a car bomb attack last October that injured one of the island's judges and his five-year-old daughter. Andreas Onoufriou of Limassol was arrested in the eastern British port of Hull on Thursday by British detectives, in close touch with Cypriot authorities, who want him extradited to Cyprus. "He was charged with various offences including the attempted murder of a district judge and his daughter in October 1996," a police spokeswoman said.
Judge Michalis Mavronikolas, 41, was approaching his car, parked in the drive of his Limassol home, to take his triplet daughters to school when the bomb exploded.
One of his daughters, Marina, suffered minor burns and was taken to hospital in a state of shock, while Mavronikolas had to undergo surgery for leg injuries.
Mavronikolas did not normally handle criminal cases. But just before the attack he issued two remand orders on suspects suspected of criminal offences.
A series of bombings have shaken Limassol, a bustling port city where criminal gangs are believed to be waging a turf war over brothels and extortion rackets.
